However, they are relevant because this man is a newspaper reporter, and if he has strongly indicated that his bias was there and his participation is to punish or to help the authorities to punish the Serbs for what they have done, and that he has discarded his code of newspaper reporters to be impartial in these conflicts, I think his previous notes are relevant, just as notes of any other witness, to show his inconsistency. If he is changing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vucicevic. I think we just wanted to find out if you're maintaining that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do, and for the reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There was another motion that I submitted and that was basically related to the events we discussed today, so I would ask that that motion just be included, but it's covered with everything that was discussed today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: There is a practical matter I'd like to raise, if I may, please. Depending on what decision you come to in relation to the motion you've been dealing with this morning, if you admit the transcripts, whether subject to or not subject to cross-examination, the witnesses produced during the course of their transcript evidence the exhibits. I assume that those exhibits will accompany those portions of the transcripts which are admitted. But I haven't seen any reference to what should happen to the exhibits, and there is nothing in the rules about what should happen to exhibits, so it may be that's a matter that Your Honours need to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ryneveld?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Well, many of those exhibits, of course, are -- have been entered in other proceedings and the transcript actually gives the witness's impression about -- formed from having seen those particular exhibits. If the court deems it necessary, we can prepare a binder of those exhibits from other transcripts. However, they have not been included with the material that we have presented to the court. In other words, these could be binders of material with respect to Mr. Vulliamy and Judge Greve. I believe they made specific reference to exhibit numbers in other proceedings. In the event that the court requires those exhibits, then we will have to tender those at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are you seeking their admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I hadn't anticipated the necessity to do so. However, if the court finds that the evidence relied upon by the Prosecution is meaningless without reference to those, we can belatedly ask to tender them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So at the moment the state of the evidence is -- the state of the application is that you're not applying for admission of the exhibits, you're merely applying for admission of the transcripts?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So if the Defence wanted at any time exhibits admitted, they could no doubt ask for them?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. And if the court requires assistance, all we need is an instruction from the court, but it's not my application at this time to include those exhibits with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The thought I have is this - and I'm not trying to be a contentious here. You're admitting the evidence. The evidence that was given at the trial is not just that which is said but it's the adoption by the witness of, "I see an exhibit. It's an exhibit I recognised and I have prepared and I have relied on it in drawing the conclusions to which I have come." And therefore, the evidence that you admit cannot be complete potentially unless you also have the exhibits upon which that witness has relied. It's not so much a matter of the Defence wanting things in and not, it's "Is that evidence complete in the way it's being presented to you?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You say the exhibits are concomitant with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: They're effectively part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take that into consideration. We will adjourn now, and we will resume next Tuesday at 9.30

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 1st day of May, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
